Ang Mo Kio

Ang Mo Kio 87

  1. Must see · Bak Kut Teh & Soups · Ang Mo Kio

    Xi Xiang Feng Yong Tau Foo

    Reliably the longest queue at 724 AMK Central — a half-hour wait even off-peak — for a yong tau foo rated among the island's best, its handmade pieces defined by a deeply savoury house sauce; order it over chee cheong fun (S$0.80) or as laksa (S$3). Widely reviewed by ieatishootipost, Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook and Seth Lui.

    Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-23, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Miss Tam Chiak, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Johor Kaki (Tony Boey), Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg, Cavin Teo (Entree Kibbles)

  2. Must see · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Ang Mo Kio

    Plum Village

    Widely called Singapore's oldest Hakka restaurant (going back to 1960s Chin Swee Road, at Jalan Leban on the Sembawang Hills/AMK fringe for over 30 years) — the abacus seeds are pounded with more yam than flour and wok-fried with dried shrimp, minced pork and mushroom, alongside stuffed beancurd, khong bak and festive poon choi.

    16 Jalan Leban, Singapore 577554

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak, Ordinary Patrons, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey), Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost)

  3. Must see · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Ang Mo Kio Fried Kway Teow

    An elderly couple has fried this heritage char kway teow for 40-odd years, opening just 3.5 hours a day — the longest queue in 724 AMK Central, with senior regulars waiting 30 minutes at lunch for smoky, lard-slicked plates.

    Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-22, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Miss Tam Chiak, Daniel Food Diary

  4. Must see · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Malaysian Hup Kee Fishball Noodle

    Two brothers from Kuantan scrape yellowtail by hand daily — fishballs of pure fish, salt and pepper with no flour or filler, tossed Malaysian-style with black sauce and shallot oil. Sells out within four hours; closed Mondays.

    Blk 158 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, #01-590 (coffeeshop beside Mayflower Market), S560158

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook.sg, Mothership

  5. Must see · Chilli Crab & Seafood · Ang Mo Kio

    Mellben Seafood

    A crab specialist since 1979 (Michelin Plate 2019) whose signature claypot crab bee hoon simmers over 20 crab shells into a rich, sweet milky broth soaked into glass noodles — plus chilli, black pepper and salted-egg crabs. Come early; the queue forms fast.

    Blk 232 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-1222, S560232

    Recommended by MICHELIN Guide, Daniel Food Diary, Eatbook.sg, HungryGoWhere

  6. Must see · Malay & Nasi Padang · Ang Mo Kio

    Rahim Muslim Food

    Around since 1957 and now third-generation, Rahim's Straits Times-featured 'Power' mee rebus layers savoury satay peanut sauce and spiced chicken over the usual gravy — long queues at this Chong Boon stall for mee rebus and mee soto.

    Chong Boon Market & Food Centre, #01-01, Blk 453A Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560453

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak

  7. Must see · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Hup Hup Minced Meat Noodle

    A Michelin Guide-listed old-school minced meat noodle at 724 AMK Central — springy mee pok or mee kia tossed in a distinctive ketchup-forward chilli sauce with minced pork, braised mushroom and a round cracker, from S$3. Loaded portions and one of the heartland's most-cited bak chor mee stalls.

    Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-39, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Seth Lui, Her World Singapore, The Singapore Women's Weekly

  8. Must see · Ang Mo Kio

    Ang Mo Kio Town Garden West

    Completed in 1983 as the HDB's largest town-garden project of its day (~21 ha), built on a hillock with spreading greenery, a lotus pond home to some 19 dragonfly species, and a lookout — a pioneering piece of heartland landscaping and an Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail site. (Note: a section near the pond is affected by LTA's North-South Corridor works.)

    Look for Open daily, free

    Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5 / Avenue 6 (opposite Ang Mo Kio Public Library), Singapore

    Recommended by NParks (National Parks Board), Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia

  9. Must see · Malay & Nasi Padang · Ang Mo Kio

    Yunos N Family

    Started by the late Haji Yunos Ahmad as a 1965 pushcart at Hastings Road and now run by the third generation, this stall pours a thick, spiced sweet-potato mee rebus gravy that ranks among Singapore's most storied — also known for its satay and soto.

    Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-01, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak

  10. Must see · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Ang Mo Kio

    Ho Bee Roasted Food

    AMK's most popular roast-meat stall for two decades, drawing long queues for glossy char siew, shatter-crisp sio bak and a paper-skinned roast duck that fans rate above town shops — the classic combo plate is S$4.50.

    Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, #01-84, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook.sg

  11. Must see · Indian & Roti Prata · Ang Mo Kio

    Sin Ming Roti Prata

    On the Sin Ming edge of AMK, this corner stall traces back to a 1933 street-prata grandfather; the third generation flips 19 kinds and a famed hand-rolled Coin Prata set (S$4 for 6) that queues form for at breakfast.

    Jin Fa Kopitiam, Blk 24 Sin Ming Road, #01-51, S570024

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Daniel Food Diary, Miss Tam Chiak

  12. Must see · Indian & Roti Prata · Ang Mo Kio

    Thasevi Food (Famous Jalan Kayu Prata)

    The stall that made 'Jalan Kayu prata' a Singapore byword — serving small, round, crispy prata (plus murtabak, mee goreng and biryani) since the 1960s, so copied that it signboards itself the 'Original Prata Shop'. Open 24 hours.

    237 Jalan Kayu, S799462

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), The Honeycombers Singapore, Ordinary Patrons

  13. Must see · Ang Mo Kio

    Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park

    One of Singapore's largest heartland parks and a global model for river restoration — under the ABC Waters Programme, a 2.7 km concrete stormwater canal was torn out and rebuilt as a 3 km meandering naturalised Kallang River. A 2017-19 NUS study found the naturalised river lifted the park's biodiversity by 33% (197 animal species, incl. 59 birds and 22 dragonflies).

    Look for Open 24h, free

    1380 Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, Singapore 569930

    Recommended by NParks (National Parks Board), PUB, Singapore's National Water Agency

  14. Must see · Ang Mo Kio

    Kebun Baru Birdsinging Club

    Singapore's largest bird-singing and display arena — established 1987 from a 1970s gathering of three AMK zebra-dove keepers, it holds more than a thousand cages on 20-foot poles rigged with pulleys across a space the size of two football fields. A rare surviving fragment of kampong-era culture and a stop on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail.

    Look for Morning sessions (esp. weekends), free

    Block 159A, Ang Mo Kio Ave 5 (foot of Ang Mo Kio Town Garden West), Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), TheSmartLocal

  15. Worth the detour · Kaya Toast, Kopitiam & Breakfast · Ang Mo Kio

    Sin Hoe Huat Cafe

    A traditional kopi-and-toast stall serving breakfast since 1968, now run by a third-generation mother-and-son duo — award-winning homemade kaya with a strong coconut aroma slathered on soft, crisp-edged 'Emperor' buns, paired with sous-vide eggs and old-school kopi.

    Sembawang Hills Food Centre, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419

    Recommended by ladyironchef (Brad Lau), Miss Tam Chiak, The Singapore Women's Weekly, Her World Singapore, Daniel Food Diary

  16. Worth the detour · Ang Mo Kio

    Old Upper Thomson Road (Thomson Road Grand Prix Circuit)

    The surviving loop of the former Thomson Road Grand Prix circuit that hosted the Singapore Grand Prix from 1961 to 1973 — a ~4.8 km course legendary for its danger, with corners nicknamed Devil's Bend, The Snakes and Murder Mile. Now a quiet cycling and walking road on the AMK/Thomson fringe, part of it threading through Thomson Nature Park alongside the old Hainan-village ruins.

    Look for Open road; free to walk/cycle

    Old Upper Thomson Road (through/around Thomson Nature Park), Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, National Library Board, Atlas Obscura, Remember Singapore

  17. Worth the detour · Cafés & Modern · Ang Mo Kio

    Twenty Grammes

    The heartland flagship of the North Bridge Road dessert cafe, doing waffle-and-ice-cream sets in an AMK void deck — the charcoal waffle with salted-egg drizzle (S$8.50), an AMK-exclusive 'Yuan Yang' half-charcoal-half-Belgian waffle, and a toasted-marshmallow S'mores waffle (S$15). Open late on weekends.

    Blk 529 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, #01-2353, S560529

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, ladyironchef (Brad Lau), Daniel Food Diary

  18. Worth the detour · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Ang Mo Kio

    Belinda's Pancake

    Aunty Belinda's morning stall at Teck Ghee Court is prized for min jiang kueh with a generous filling-to-pancake ratio (peanut, coconut or red bean), a crisp cone-crepe version, and putu mayam (S$1.80 for two). Often sold out before noon.

    Teck Ghee Court Market & Food Centre, #01-27, Blk 341 Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, S560341

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, HungryGoWhere

  19. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Shu Heng Bi Tai Mak

    A perpetual pre-lunch queue at Kebun Baru since Dec 2020 for a Johor-Bahru-style bi tai mak (S$4) rarely found this side of the Causeway — freshly-made 'rat-tail' noodles in a viscous, gravy-like broth crossing robust pork stock with light ikan bilis, studded with minced pork, mushroom, hae bee, garlic, fried shallots and salted fish. Sells out before lunch.

    Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Street 22, S560226 (stall no. to confirm)

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey), Miss Tam Chiak

  20. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Lai Heng Char Kway Teow

    A Sembawang Hills favourite (formerly at Shunfu/Lakeview) for a wet, wok-hei char kway teow with cockles, beansprouts and Chinese sausage from S$3, best paired with its smoky S$1 otah. Closed Mondays.

    Sembawang Hills Food Centre, #01-32, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey)

  21. Worth the detour · Ang Mo Kio

    Thomson Nature Park

    Singapore's 7th nature park (opened 2019), built around the atmospheric ruins of a 1930s-60s Hainanese village and a key conservation site for the critically endangered Raffles' banded langur. Five trails (3.8 km) — Ruins and Figs, Stream and Ferns, Rambutan, Langur and Macaque — wind past old village foundations and troops of long-tailed macaques.

    Look for 7am-7pm, free

    Upper Thomson Road (near Springleaf), Singapore

    Recommended by NParks (National Parks Board), Little Day Out, TheSmartLocal

  22. Worth the detour · Ang Mo Kio

    Church of Christ the King

    The only Catholic church in Ang Mo Kio — its foundation stone laid in 1981 by Archbishop Gregory Yong, it cost around S$3 million (then twice any other church in Singapore) and opened in 1982 before being rebuilt in 2002. Marked on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail; the facade carries a statue of Christ the King.

    Look for Free entry

    2221 Ang Mo Kio Ave 8, Singapore 569809

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia, CATHOLICSG

  23. Worth the detour · Ang Mo Kio

    Ang Mo Kio Dragon Playground

    One of the last surviving vintage sand-pit dragon playgrounds in Singapore — a 1980s reproduction of the beloved Toa Payoh design, its dragon head clad in terrazzo mosaic tiles, spine of steel rails, and (uniquely to this one) a mosaic slide. A stop on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail's Iconic Landmarks route and a nostalgic icon of heartland childhood.

    Look for Open 24h, free

    Blk 570 Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3, Singapore 560570

    Recommended by Little Day Out, Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Home & Decor Singapore

  24. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Ho Ji Fried Hokkien Mee

    Hawker Ah Ho learned the wok some 30 years ago at a famed Bukit Batok stall and now fries a leaning-wet Hokkien mee of yellow noodles and thin bee hoon in umami prawn stock — once named a top-10 Hokkien mee by Lianhe Wanbao.

    Mayflower Market & Food Centre, #01-39, Blk 162 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560162

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Seth Lui, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey)

  25. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Song Heng Fishball Minced Meat Noodle

    The longest queue at 628 with almost no publicity — a balanced chilli-vinegar dry mee pok with bouncy fishballs and a lightly sweet pork soup; fishballs regularly sell out by 11am. Closed Tuesdays.

    Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, #01-75, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey)

  26. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Ah Jie Hokkien Mee

    Two Gen-Z hawkers both named Jie fry one dish only — a wok-hei Hokkien mee on a wide stove that chars the noodles before the homemade prawn stock goes in, with fresh pork lard and house chilli. Hour-long queues since 2024.

    Food Loft Kopitiam, Ang Mo Kio Ave 8, Singapore

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  27. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Ang Mo Kio

    Kam Jia Zhuang Seafood

    A family zi char in a HDB coffeeshop since 2003, beloved for crunchy salted-egg prawns, pumpkin prawns, Dong Po pork belly and the usual chilli/salted-egg crabs — a reliable AMK feast spot.

    Blk 202 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-1690, S560202

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak

  28. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Ang Mo Kio

    Ann Hoo Teochew Porridge

    Twenty years of Teochew-style porridge and a spread of 30-plus sides — fresh fish, fried meatballs, braised pork belly — one of Cheng San's most reliable old-school stalls.

    Cheng San Market & Cooked Food Centre, Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, Singapore

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook.sg

  29. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Song Kee Fishball Noodle

    Opened by one of the sisters from the original Song Kee, this Cheng San branch draws long queues (fishballs can sell out by 1pm) for honest handmade fishballs — bouncy, not over-salted — with an enhanced fishball and beancurd skin in each bowl. Closed Mondays.

    Cheng San Market & Cooked Food Centre, #01-123, Blk 527 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560527

    Recommended by Johor Kaki (Tony Boey), Cavin Teo (Entree Kibbles), HungryGoWhere

  30. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Soi 19 Thai Wanton Mee

    A long-running Kebun Bahru stall plating Thai-style wanton noodles — al dente egg noodles lightly coated in shallot oil, springy and eggy, with fried wanton, flavourful char siew and crisp pork lard. A dish rarely found outside Thailand and a longtime AMK draw.

    Blk 151 Ang Mo Kio Ave 5, #01-05, S560151

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Cavin Teo (Entree Kibbles), Eatbook.sg

  31. Worth the detour · Cafés & Modern · Ang Mo Kio

    Rasa Sayang Western Food

    An old-school hawker-Western institution first opened in 1994 (originally at Blk 711 Ave 8) that reappeared at Blk 347 in 2021 to steady queues — thin, crispy chicken cutlet, pork chop, fish and chips and sirloin steak at heartland prices, in the Hainanese-Western tradition. Closed Wednesdays.

    Blk 347 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-2142, S560347

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  32. Worth the detour · Laksa & Curry Noodles · Ang Mo Kio

    Hong Heng Beef Noodle Soup & Laksa

    A rare stall selling both beef noodles and laksa under one roof — and, unusually, a Mixed Beef Laksa (S$5.50) that spoons coconut-rich laksa gravy over tender beef. Also a dry beef noodle with thick bee hoon and a fresh-cockles laksa. Relocated to Kebun Baru from AMK Ave 3; closed Mondays.

    Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, #01-16, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Street 22, S560226

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook.sg

  33. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Ang Mo Kio

    Ayah Dimsum

    A Muslim-owned dim sum stall (sharing a coffeeshop with Friends Kitchen HK, whose team co-owns it) doing an unusually wide handmade range from S$2.50 — chunky chicken-and-shrimp siew mai, fluffy BBQ chicken buns and salted-egg lava buns — a genuine rarity as halal dim sum in the heartland.

    Blk 260 Ang Mo Kio Street 21, S560260

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Have Halal Will Travel (HHWT), 8days (Mediacorp)

  34. Worth the detour · Ang Mo Kio

    Ang Mo Kio Town Garden East

    The eastern counterpart town garden, tucked behind Ang Mo Kio MRT at the junction of Avenues 3 and 8 — a landscaped neighbourhood green with ponds and rest areas serving the surrounding HDB blocks.

    Look for Open daily, free

    Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3 / Avenue 8 (behind Ang Mo Kio MRT), Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, NParks (National Parks Board)

  35. Worth the detour · Ang Mo Kio

    Windsor Nature Park

    A 75-ha nature park opened in 2017 on the AMK/Upper Thomson fringe, a quieter gateway into the Central Catchment. About 4 km of trails — the boardwalked Hanguana Trail over a freshwater swamp forest, the Venus Loop and Drongo Trail — link to MacRitchie and the TreeTop Walk.

    Look for 7am-7pm, free

    30 Venus Drive, Singapore 573858

    Recommended by NParks (National Parks Board), The Travel Intern

  36. Worth the detour · Ang Mo Kio

    MacRitchie TreeTop Walk

    A 250 m free-standing suspension bridge strung between MacRitchie's two highest points, Bukit Peirce and Bukit Kalang, high in the rainforest canopy — reached on foot from the AMK-side Venus Drive / Windsor trailheads. Closed Mondays (except public holidays).

    Look for Tue-Fri 9am-5pm, wknd 8:30am-5pm; free

    Central Catchment Nature Reserve (via Venus Drive, off Upper Thomson Road), Singapore

    Recommended by NParks (National Parks Board), The Travel Intern

  37. Worth the detour · Ang Mo Kio

    Lower Peirce Reservoir Park

    A park around Singapore's second-oldest reservoir (1910s) whose 900 m nature boardwalk, built in 1998 along existing trails, threads one of the island's last mature secondary forests at the water's edge — home to more than 900 flowering plants, 100 ferns and 250 animal species.

    Look for Open daily, free

    Casuarina Road / Upper Thomson Road, Singapore

    Recommended by NParks (National Parks Board), Wikipedia

  38. Worth the detour · Ang Mo Kio

    Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail

    NHB's self-guided trail through Singapore's quintessential heartland town — refreshed in 2023 to 40 heritage sites and 10 markers across three routes (Iconic Landmarks, Hidden Heartland Gems, Scenic Fringes), linking the Clover Block, Kebun Baru Birdsinging Club, Chu Sheng Temple, Church of Christ the King, Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park and more.

    Look for Free; maps on Roots.gov.sg

    Ang Mo Kio Town Centre (trail markers islandwide across AMK), Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), National Heritage Board

  39. Worth the detour · Ang Mo Kio

    Block 259, the 'Clover Block'

    The only block of circular flats the HDB ever built — four round towers joined into a four-leaf-clover plan (completed 1981), part of a late-1970s pilot of seven distinctively designed blocks meant to give estates their own identity. Built in solid brick with round rooms larger than a standard five-room flat; now an AMK icon and a heritage-trail marker.

    Look for Residential; view from ground level

    259 Ang Mo Kio Avenue 2, Singapore 560259

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia

    Imperial Fish Soup

    Millennial hawker Max left a finance job in 2020 and, after training at Hock Heng, opened this long-queue stall; the Signature Seafood Noodle (from S$5) plays like bak chor mee but with seafood in place of pork.

    Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628

    Kian Seng Seafood Restaurant

    No Horse Run Cafe

    Centre Satay Bee Hoon

    Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-12, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724

    Recommended by Her World Singapore, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey)

  46. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Ang Mo Kio

    Huang Fu Duck Rice

    Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, #01-20, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, S560226

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak

  47. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Jing Ji Fishball Noodle

    Sembawang Hills' standout fishball noodle — a dry mee pok tossed in a house blend of chilli, vinegar and tomato, with fishballs, fishcake and pork liver served in a light porky soup.

    Sembawang Hills Food Centre, #01-04, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary

  48. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Ang Mo Kio

    Han Jiang Fish Soup

    A two-brother sliced-fish soup stall at 409 (Teck Ghee Square) whose broth balances savoury, sweet and a tang from fresh tomato, layered with tee po (dried sole), soy beans, tofu and seaweed. The queue runs 30 minutes even off-peak; soup from S$5.50, +S$0.50 with bee hoon.

    409 AMK Market & Food Centre, #01-15, Blk 409 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560409

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey)

  49. Worth the detour · Indian & Roti Prata · Ang Mo Kio

    Casuarina Curry

    One of Singapore's most famous prata houses, on the Casuarina Road / Lower Peirce fringe of AMK — light, ghee-fragrant prata across 60-plus flavours (from Alfredo to salted-egg prawn), plus fish head curry, biryani, thosai and the off-menu R.K. Special (prata in mutton curry with soft-boiled eggs). Open till late.

    136-138 Casuarina Road, Singapore 579526

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Time Out Singapore

  50. Worth the detour · Vietnamese · Ang Mo Kio

    Crunch & Cups

    A hidden Vietnamese nook in a new AMK BTO estate — a crunchy, well-stuffed Saigon banh mi (S$6.90) with pork floss and meats, plus a milky, subtly savoury ice salted coffee (S$4.90). Small, cash-and-carry, and a genuine rarity in the heartland.

    Blk 260 Ang Mo Kio Street 21, #01-04, S560260

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  51. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    3 Sisters Prawn Noodle

    A humble Mayflower stall run by three sisters, doing a comforting prawn mee alongside fried Hokkien mee at value prices with generous prawns — friendly service and moderate waits. Opens from 6am; closed Wednesdays.

    Mayflower Market & Food Centre, #01-06, Blk 162 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560162

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Seth Lui

  52. Worth the detour · Hainanese Chicken Rice · Ang Mo Kio

    Mun Fu Chicken Rice

    Founded in 1992 and run by a father and his two sons, this perpetually-queued Cheng San stall poaches its chicken the traditional way — an ice bath sets the gelatin under the skin for a slippery, slightly fatty finish — and debones it for you. Plates around S$4.50.

    Cheng San Market & Cooked Food Centre, #01-110, Blk 527 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560527

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost)

  53. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Seletar Sheng Mian & Mian Fen Guo

    A perpetual-queue stall at Kebun Baru for hand-torn mee hoon kueh and hand-pulled sheng mian, the noodles the pride of the house, in a broth boiled with pork bones and ikan bilis for a natural sweetness. Dry or soup, S$4-6.

    Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, #01-07, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Street 22, S560226

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak

  54. Worth the detour · Cafés & Modern · Ang Mo Kio

    F.I.C

    A cosy void-deck cafe (Fried Ice Cream) that pairs its signature fried ice cream with Vietnamese-leaning bites — an unpretentious neighbourhood dessert-and-coffee spot that made both Eatbook's and HungryGoWhere's Ang Mo Kio round-ups.

    Ang Mo Kio (void-deck cafe; exact block to confirm at geocode)

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, HungryGoWhere

  55. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Eng Ho Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee

    A wetter, prawn-stock-drenched fried Hokkien mee at 409 (Teck Ghee Square) built on a rich stock of wild sea prawns (swa lor), squid and pork for a sweeter, more delicate depth. Fried in batches with 30-40 minute peak-hour waits; named a top-10 Hokkien mee in Singapore by Lianhe Wanbao. Opens 4pm, closed alternate Tuesdays.

    409 AMK Market & Food Centre (Teck Ghee Square), #01-34, Blk 409 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560409

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak

  56. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    Zhen Ming Pork Ribs Prawn Noodle

    A 20-plus-year Mayflower stall whose brown prawn broth is simmered at least six hours with pork ribs, pig skin, red dates, prawn shells and black sugarcane (in place of rock sugar) for a natural, addictive sweetness — served dry or soup with fishcake, lean meat, Brazilian pork ribs and prawns. Mornings only; closed Tuesdays.

    Mayflower Market & Food Centre, #01-04, Blk 162 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560162

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Seth Lui

  57. Worth the detour · Indian & Roti Prata · Ang Mo Kio

    Thohirah Restaurant

    A 24-hour Jalan Kayu institution on the AMK/Seletar fringe serving Singaporean, Malay, Thai and South Indian fare — famed for its prata, biryani, satay and curry fish head, with an air-conditioned wing alongside the coffeeshop seating. Packed at breakfast and supper.

    258 Jalan Kayu, S799487

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak

  58. Worth the detour · Cafés & Modern · Ang Mo Kio

    Dongsheng Cafe

    A 2025-opened old-school Nanyang cafe doing classic heartland fare — mani cai (sayur manis) mee hoon kueh, laksa, steamed toast and frothy kopi, most mains under S$8, CDC vouchers accepted. Open daily 7am-10pm.

    Blk 163 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, #01-414, S560163

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

  59. Worth the detour · Cafés & Modern · Ang Mo Kio

    Wonders

    A void-deck gelato cafe themed around mahjong — flavours inspired by Chinese sweets, served with Belgian waffles, croffles and pandan-mochi or nian gao waffles, the tiles motif carried playfully through the shop. Open till late on weekends.

    Blk 128 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-1867, S560128

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary

  60. Deep cut · Ang Mo Kio

    Masjid Al-Muttaqin

    Ang Mo Kio's HDB-built neighbourhood mosque, opened 21 September 1980 for a community that had earlier prayed at Thomson Road and Kampong Sireh. Part-funded by MUIS with the rest raised by residents through donations and food fairs, it accommodates up to 3,500 worshippers and is a marker on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail.

    Look for Free entry

    5140 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, Singapore 569844

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia, MUIS (Islamic Religious Council of Singapore)

  61. Deep cut · Ang Mo Kio

    Ang Mo Kio Joint Temple

    Established in 1978 and rebuilt in 2011, this joint temple houses three deities' temples displaced when their villages were cleared in the 1970s — Gao Lin Gong, Kim Eang Tong and Leng San Giam. The oldest, Gao Lin Gong, was founded in 1888 by Huang-surname immigrants from Nan An, Fujian, at Kow Tiow Kio ('nine bridges') along today's Ang Mo Kio Avenue 1; its pillars and facade carry carvings handcrafted by artisans in China. An Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail hidden gem.

    Look for Free entry

    Ang Mo Kio Avenue 1 vicinity, Singapore (Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail; exact street to confirm)

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), National Heritage Board, SG Magazine

  62. Deep cut · Ang Mo Kio

    Sembawang Hills Estate

    A private landed estate on the AMK/Upper Thomson fringe, jointly developed in the 1950s by Bukit Sembawang Rubber Estates and Singapore United Rubber Estates as rubber companies pivoted from a declining plantation trade into housing — one of the earliest such estates. A Scenic Fringes marker on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail, and home to the well-loved Sembawang Hills Food Centre.

    Look for Residential estate; free to walk

    Sembawang Hills Estate (Jalan Leban / Upper Thomson Road vicinity), Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia, National Heritage Board

  63. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Ang Mo Kio

    Kuai San Dian Xin

    A no-frills 24-hour spot where every basket of dim sum is S$1.30 (buy 10, get 1 free) — fried prawn dumplings and siew mai the picks; not fine dining, but unbeatable value.

    Blk 555 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, #01-1936, S560555

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak, HungryGoWhere

  64. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Ang Mo Kio

    Seng Huat Duck Rice

    A long-loved, no-frills braised duck rice and porridge counter at Sembawang Hills, a Thomson-and-Sembawang neighbourhood standby featured across the centre's guides.

    Sembawang Hills Food Centre, #01-27, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Daniel Food Diary, Seth Lui

  65. Deep cut · Cafés & Modern · Ang Mo Kio

    Ki-mochi

    An under-HDB dessert cafe doing chewy mochi pancakes, mochi waffles and gelato at nett prices (from S$4.50), open late on weekends — a 14-minute walk from AMK MRT. (Status to re-verify: one report suggests the unit has since changed hands.)

    Blk 446 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, #01-1661, S560446

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, Mothership

  66. Deep cut · Ang Mo Kio

    Chu Sheng Temple

    A Hokkien-style temple built in 1981 to house three older village temples — Ji Fu Gong, Hua Tang Fu and Long Quan Yan — displaced from Yio Chu Kang's 11th milestone (Ka Tau Au) by redevelopment. Pronounced curved roof ridges mark its Hokkien architecture; former villagers still gather here and it runs community charity. An Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail hidden gem.

    Look for Free entry

    48 Ang Mo Kio Street 61, Singapore 569163

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), National Heritage Board

  67. Deep cut · Ang Mo Kio

    Liuxun Sanhemiao

    Completed in 1989, this joint temple unites three temples — Sam Ann Fu, Longxuyan Jinshuiguan and the Hong San Chin Huat Temple Association — that once stood at Lak Xun, a village in Yio Chu Kang near present-day Lentor Avenue. One of two new markers added to the refreshed Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail in 2023, recording the town's transformation from plantation land to new town.

    Look for Free entry

    Ang Mo Kio / Yio Chu Kang vicinity (near Lentor Avenue), Singapore (Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail)

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), National Heritage Board

  68. Deep cut · Ang Mo Kio

    Swee Kow Kuan

    A clan temple and association for people of the Hong (Xiong) surname, first established in 1905 at Buona Vista and relocated over the decades to Ang Mo Kio — a rare surviving surname-clan temple and a Hidden Heartland Gems stop on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail, illustrating the village-and-clan networks that predate the new town.

    Look for Free entry

    Ang Mo Kio (Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail hidden gem; exact street to confirm)

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), National Heritage Board

  69. Deep cut · Ang Mo Kio

    Teachers' Housing Estate

    A landed estate developed by the Singapore Teachers' Union — completed 1969 and officially opened in 1971 by then-Education Minister Lim Kim San — whose roads are named after literary figures such as Tu Fu, Rabindranath Tagore and Munshi Abdullah. A Scenic Fringes marker on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail.

    Look for Residential estate; free to walk

    Teachers' Estate (off Jalan Kuras / Upper Thomson, Yio Chu Kang side), Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), National Heritage Board

    Seng Bee Hainanese Chicken Rice

    A traditional Hainanese chicken rice counter that regularly makes the round-ups of 724 AMK Central's best — poached chicken and fragrant rice at heartland prices.

    Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

    A value-for-money wanton mee whose secret is in the lard-based sauce — springy egg noodles loaded with braised chicken feet, char siew and crispy pork lard bits. A long-standing local favourite carried over from its Blk 453 origins.

    A homely Thai stall (also in Toa Payoh) plating authentic street-Thai — a prawn-generous seafood tom yum nam kun (S$6.50), green curry with prawns, papaya salad and a peppery claypot tanghoon with prawns that stays springy. Affordable and consistently recommended.

  85. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Ang Mo Kio

    A husband-and-wife fishball noodle stall of some 30 years at Cheng San — a lardy, savoury-tangy fishball kway teow soup (from S$4) with minced meat, mushroom, pork lard and fresh liver, its in-house chilli of dried chillies and shallots giving a fiery kick.     A 724 AMK Central Western stall going since the 1990s, a longstanding heartland pick for grilled and deep-fried meats — chicken, pork chop and steak — in the old-school Hainanese-Western tradition. Opens afternoons, closed Mondays.

  87. Closed — kept for the record · Cafés & Modern · Ang Mo Kio

    Grub — CLOSED

    A family-friendly bistro set midway through Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park with an alfresco deck over the greenery — Asian-twist brunch of har cheong gai and waffles, truffled egg cocotte, mentaiko fries and a sustainable-fish crispy burger, with craft brews. Around S$22/pax; go early before the queue.

How this guide was made
